nodes.label: Arbor: Autonomous Research via Hypothesis-Tree Refinement
nodes.author: Jiajie Jin et al.
nodes.rationale: Arbor is a framework for autonomous optimization that combines a long-lived coordinator, short-lived executors, and Hypothesis Tree Refinement to turn autonomous research into cumulative hypothesis refinement.

nodes.label: Autonomous Optimization (AO): Long-Horizon Research Task Class
nodes.author: Jiajie Jin et al.
nodes.rationale: AO formalizes autonomous research as iterative artifact improvement through experimental feedback without step-level human supervision; captures core operational form of research.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Tree Refinement (HTR): Persistent Research State
nodes.author: Jiajie Jin et al.
nodes.rationale: HTR represents research as a persistent tree where each node binds hypothesis, artifact version, experimental evidence, and distilled insight; tree acts as search frontier, memory, and audit trail.

nodes.label: Arbor Coordinator: Long-Lived Research State Manager
nodes.author: Jiajie Jin et al.
nodes.rationale: Coordinator owns global research state and decides how search frontier evolves; maintains hypothesis tree, observes results, ideates new hypotheses, selects promising directions, and makes merge/prune decisions.

nodes.label: Arbor Executor: Short-Lived Hypothesis Implementer
nodes.author: Jiajie Jin et al.
nodes.rationale: Executors test individual hypotheses in isolated worktrees and return structured evidence; short-lived nature allows parallel exploration and prevents context explosion.

nodes.label: MLE-Bench Lite: Machine Learning Engineering Benchmark
nodes.author: Jiajie Jin et al.
nodes.rationale: MLE-Bench Lite is used to evaluate Arbor; Arbor reaches 86.36% Any Medal with GPT-5.5, the strongest result in comparison.

nodes.label: Six AO Tasks: Model Training, Harness Engineering, Data Synthesis
nodes.author: Jiajie Jin et al.
nodes.rationale: Six real research tasks from model training, harness engineering, and data synthesis; Arbor achieves best held-out result on all six with 2.5× average relative gain over Codex and Claude Code.

nodes.label: Arbor: Autonomous Optimization Framework
nodes.rationale: Framework for autonomous research using hypothesis tree refinement to organize long-horizon experimental exploration with persistent state management, separating global strategy from local execution.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Tree Refinement (HTR)
nodes.rationale: Core mechanism for maintaining research state as a persistent tree structure where nodes bind hypotheses, artifacts, evidence, and insights; enables cumulative exploration rather than isolated trials.

nodes.label: Coordinator Agent
nodes.rationale: Long-lived agent that owns the hypothesis tree and makes strategic decisions: observing frontier, ideating candidates, selecting experiments, dispatching executors, backpropagating insights, and deciding on merges/prunes.

nodes.label: Executor Agent
nodes.rationale: Short-lived agent that implements a single hypothesis in an isolated worktree, evaluates it on development set, and returns structured evidence (score, result, insight, branch reference) without modifying shared tree.

nodes.label: Held-Out Merge Gate
nodes.rationale: Mechanism that separates exploratory improvement on development evaluator from verified artifact-level progress; candidate promoted to current best only if it improves on held-out test evaluator.

nodes.label: Autonomous Optimization (AO)
nodes.rationale: Problem formulation where agent improves a mutable artifact through long-horizon experimental feedback; defined as tuple (M₀, O, E_dev, E_test) with development and held-out evaluators.

nodes.label: AO Task Suite
nodes.rationale: Six real research tasks spanning model training (Optimizer Design, Architecture Design), harness engineering (Terminal-Bench 2.0, BrowseComp), and data synthesis (Search-Agent, Math-Reasoning).

nodes.label: Optimizer Design Task
nodes.rationale: NanoGPT-Bench task: minimize training steps to reach target validation loss; tests agent's ability to improve optimizer efficiency under expensive experimental feedback.

nodes.label: Architecture Design Task
nodes.rationale: autoresearch benchmark: minimize final validation loss under fixed time budget by modifying LLM training codebase; tests discovery of algorithmic improvements.

nodes.label: Terminal-Bench 2.0 Task
nodes.rationale: Harness engineering task: improve terminal agent pass rate on command-line tasks; tests agent's ability to optimize control logic around another agent.

nodes.label: BrowseComp Task
nodes.rationale: Harness engineering task: improve search agent accuracy on browsing questions; tests discovery of harness-level changes that transfer to unseen tasks.

nodes.label: Search-Agent Data Synthesis Task
nodes.rationale: Data synthesis task: improve quality of generated search-intensive QA items; scores items solvable under repeated attempts but not on first attempt.

nodes.label: Math-Reasoning Data Synthesis Task
nodes.rationale: Data synthesis task: improve generation of AIME-style contest problems; tests discovery of calibration and filtering mechanisms.

nodes.label: MLE-Bench Lite
nodes.rationale: Established long-horizon ML engineering benchmark used for comparison against reported baseline systems; tests transfer of Arbor controller to official benchmark protocol.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Refinement Analysis
nodes.rationale: Analysis showing hypothesis refinement as deepening of task understanding: early nodes test broad mechanisms, later nodes identify limits, ancestor insights compress results into constraints.

nodes.label: Search Efficiency Analysis
nodes.rationale: Analysis showing strong candidates often appear mid-to-late in runs after earlier nodes establish mechanisms and constraints; efficiency measured by reduced arbitrariness of later search.

nodes.label: Idea Quality Analysis
nodes.rationale: Analysis showing useful ideas are local, executable, and evidence-conditioned; successful proposals directly respond to earlier observations and failure modes.

nodes.label: Tree Structure Ablation
nodes.rationale: Ablation removing hierarchical tree structure reduces performance from 81.82% to 63.64% any-medal rate; shows tree improves refinement rather than basic executability.

nodes.label: Insight Feedback Ablation
nodes.rationale: Ablation disabling upward propagation of insights reduces performance from 81.82% to 54.54%; shows semantic memory from insight feedback is essential for later decisions.

nodes.label: Token Consumption Analysis
nodes.rationale: Analysis showing Arbor uses 20-43M tokens comparable to baselines but achieves larger held-out gains; improvement from structured search organization rather than larger sampling.

nodes.label: Cross-Task Transfer Study
nodes.rationale: BrowseComp-optimized harness transfers to unseen tasks (HLE, DeepSearchQA) without task-specific optimization; demonstrates discovery of generally useful design changes.

nodes.label: Backbone Model Generality
nodes.rationale: Arbor achieves gains with Gemini-3-Flash, Claude Opus 4.6, and GPT-5.5; framework is model-agnostic though empirical ceiling depends on task-backbone fit.
